extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant reviewers and researchers in C. elegans antiviral immunity / molecular genetics
extracted.subtask_description: Experimental design and methodological standards for dissecting DRH-1/RLR-mediated antiviral signaling in C. elegans, including transgenic strategies, loss/gain-of-function assays, proteomics, forward genetics, and single-cell transcriptomics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boosting wrmScarlet expression strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: If expression is very dim with the initial approach or absent with the 'non-split' wrmScarlet approach, generate a drh-1 promoter::drh-1 cDNA::unc-54 3'UTR construct and insert as single-copy into the genome and as multi-copy extrachromosomal array; adding an unc-54 3'UTR has been successful in boosting expression in many other studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If still unsuccessful, use existing ubiquitously expressed rpl-28p::wrmScarlet strain to image DRH-1 subcellular distribution. As a further backup, generate a transcriptional fusion (2 kb upstream region fused to GFP, multi-copy array) because these reporters are almost always brighter than translational reporters or endogenous tagging; final fallback is to depend on existing RNAseq data for experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing drh-1 tissue distribution (reporter choice)
rubrics_metrics.description: To assess tissue distribution, generate a transcriptional fusion containing 2 kb of upstream region of the drh-1 start codon fused to GFP and examine animals containing a multi-copy extrachromosomal array.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: transcriptional reporters tend to be brighter than translational or endogenous tagging and allow better visualization of genes with lower expression; use this reporter as the basis for tissue-specific analysis if endogenous tagging is too weak.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tissue-specific rescue to determine sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Use tissue-specific promoters (e.g., vha-6 for intestine, myo-3 for muscle, rab-3 for neurons, dpy-7 for epidermis) to drive expression of drh-1 (vha-6p::wrmScarlet-3XFLAG::drh-1 etc.) introduced as single-copy via Cas-SCI to test where drh-1 is sufficient to induce the IPR upon viral infection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm tissue-specificity via wrmScarlet tag; subject strains to Orsay virus infection and measure viral load by qRT-PCR and IPR induction to assess rescue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tissue-specific depletion to determine requirement (auxin-AID)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tag endogenous drh-1 with a GFP::AID degron tag and cross with C. elegans strains that express tissue-specific TIR1 to cause tissue-specific degradation of DRH-1 (auxin-mediated protein degradation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess viral load and IPR gene expression using qRT-PCR. If issues occur (insufficient degradation or basal degradation), alternatives include the newer AID2 system or tissue-specific RNAi (not preferred due to prior issues with specificity and efficacy). Auxin-mediated depletion acts faster than RNAi and allows examination of acute effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measuring roles of candidate IPR genes in antiviral defense
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate 58 high-confidence genes (induced by Orsay infection, induced by WT RDRP expression, and drh-1 dependent) by RNAi knockdown followed by measurement of Orsay virus RNA1 levels with qRT-PCR to see if knockdown increases viral load.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow RNAi positives with gene deletions using existing knockout strains or CRISPR/Cas9. Because redundancy may mask effects in wild-type, test suppression in pals-22 mutant background (which has >10X lower viral load). Prioritize candidates (e.g., cullin-ring components, pals genes) for deeper study of expression and subcellular localization; take top five genes with greatest effect for further mechanistic analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of overexpression and mutants to infer gene function
rubrics_metrics.description: Use overexpression strains (e.g., cul-6 overexpression increases thermotolerance; pals-5 overexpression reduces protein aggregates) and analyze mutants from knockout consortium or generate CRISPR deletions to determine impact on viral load and IPR phenotypes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If RNAi or overexpression in wild-type background yields no phenotype, test in sensitized backgrounds such as pals-22 mutants and proceed to deletion analysis for higher-confidence inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterizing DRH-1-NTD effects using integrated transgenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate DRH-1-NTD::wrmScarlet transgenes into the genome (UV/psoralen integration of extrachromosomal arrays) to stabilize expression, back-cross integrated strains 3X, and confirm pals-5p::GFP expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterize integrated strains by (1) testing whether DRH-1-NTD acts upstream of ZIP-1 via zip-1 RNAi blocking pals-5p::GFP, (2) crossing into zip-1::gfp to check ZIP-1 nuclear localization, (3) perform RNAseq to compare IPR gene induction to non-transgenic, and (4) assay viral resistance using standard viral load assays. If integration fails, use COPAS Biosort to isolate transgenics for RNAseq or use FISH to analyze mosaic expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporter quantification and statistical presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantify reporter expression across life stages with biological replicates and present distributions (e.g., boxplots showing 25th–75th percentiles, median, mean).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example protocol: two independent experimental replicates, 60 animals analyzed per condition, use two-tailed t-test for significance (****p<0.0001 reported). Ensure appropriate sample sizes and replicate structure for robust inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-immunoprecipitation / Mass Spectrometry (co-IP/MS) design
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an overexpressed, tissue-specific vha-6p::wrmScarlet-3XFLAG::DRH-1 single-copy strain and a vha-6p::wrmScarlet-3XFLAG control; infect with virus or control; perform co-IP/MS with experimental triplicates using ~200,000 animals per sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform MS on a sensitive platform (e.g., UltiMate 3000 RSLCnano + Orbitrap Fusion Lumos). Identify proteins significantly interacting with DRH-1 versus control; validate highest confidence hits by RNAi knock-down followed by viral infection and measurement of IPR expression and viral load by qRT-PCR; follow positives with gene deletions for stronger evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative proximity labeling for transient interactors (TurboID)
rubrics_metrics.description: If protein-protein interactions with DRH-1 are too transient to be identified by co-IP/MS, use TurboID promiscuous biotin ligase to biotinylate proximal proteins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage prior expertise with proximity-labeling systems; include integrated DRH-1-NTD strains or endogenously tagged DRH-1 to reduce false positives associated with overexpression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation and prioritization workflow for proteomics/Y2H hits
rubrics_metrics.description: Proteomics hits should be functionally tested by RNAi and, for positive candidates, by gene deletions; cross-reference co-IP/MS hits with existing Y2H data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If RNAi yields no phenotype (possible false negatives due to incomplete knockdown), expand hit list or test deletions; consider redundancy by testing combinations; prioritize based on presence of signaling domains, localization, homology, and implication in immune responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward EMS genetic screen to identify DRH-1→ZIP-1 signaling factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the constitutive pals-5p::GFP phenotype driven by DRH-1-NTD overexpression, perform EMS mutagenesis, and identify F2 animals lacking pals-5p::GFP expression. Validate by testing endogenous pals-5 and other IPR gene expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify causative mutations with whole-genome sequencing (look for predicted loss-of-function SNPs in recessive mutants); if needed perform back-crossing, mapping, and complementation. If the screen fails (e.g., essential genes), consider a whole-genome RNAi screen as an alternative. EMS commonly identifies partial-loss-of-function alleles.

rubrics_metrics.name: scRNAseq experimental design for infected animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform single-cell RNAseq on virally infected animals in both drh-1 knockout and control backgrounds (use rde-1 mutant background to obtain higher infection rates); harvest timepoints at 8h, 16h, and 24h post infection; prepare single-cell suspensions using an optimized methanol-fixation dissociation protocol and use the 10x Genomics platform without DNA-content sorting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid DNA-content sorting because it excludes intestinal cells (which are >4N); to minimize germ cell contribution, use younger L1 animals. Use the Kenyon lab optimized dissociation protocol as a reference; plan experiments to compare infected vs uninfected cells and drh-1 dependent differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting for extracellular RNA contamination in scRNAseq
rubrics_metrics.description: Extracellular RNA from lysed cells can contaminate scRNAseq; this must be corrected to confidently call infected or responding cells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a 'barnyard' cellular spike-in approach (add a small fraction of human cells) so all C. elegans transcripts found in the 'human' fraction represent contamination, enabling direct empirical measurement and thresholding. Alternative inference methods like SoupX exist but spike-in offers direct measurement. Use these controls to derive an empiric threshold for calling bimodal on/off infections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capturing non-polyadenylated viral genomes in single-cell sequencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Orsay virus genome is non-polyadenylated and standard oligo(dT)-primed 10x approaches will not capture viral RNAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploit the 5' methyl-cap and template-switching SMARTSeq-like chemistry in 10x (and the newer 5' barcode method) by adding Orsay-specific primers to the standard 10x run to capture viral sequences concurrently with host. Validate primer/capture strategy in bulk RNAseq before scRNAseq and decide whether to amplify the 5' end only or attempt full viral cDNA capture during reverse transcription.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calling infected vs responding/bystander cells in scRNAseq
rubrics_metrics.description: Define definitively infected and definitively responding cells with empirically derived thresholds, correcting for extracellular RNA and other sample-specific artifacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because 'off' or 'uninfected' cannot be absolutely defined, use appropriate spike-ins and controls to call true positives. Aim to delineate infected cells, responding cells, and bystanders to map the structure of the transcriptional response across cell types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size and material considerations for proteomics and co-IP
rubrics_metrics.description: Proteomics/co-IP experiments require large numbers of animals and technical replicates to detect interactors of a low-expressed protein like drh-1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for substantial input (example: 200,000 animals per sample) and experimental replicates in triplicate; use sensitive mass spectrometry instrumentation and institutional core facilities (letters of support). Consider integrating transgenes or using endogenous tags to reduce false positives from overexpression.
